body.x: Organizations that run data center virtualization on VMware face licensing costs, and a growing number also want to know which country's laws govern their data. Smaller businesses, research labs and non-critical projects often need neither a complex setup nor an enterprise platform's price tag.
Altwy says it built its software for that gap.

Altwy, a French software company led by CEO Christophe Lambert, is exhibiting at KES 2026 with Access, its single-server management software. The company says Access offers a low-cost alternative to complex VMware setups and, as a fully European product, is not subject to extraterritorial laws such as the U.S. CLOUD Act or FISA. Its goals at the show are to find direct customers and Asian IT distributors and to meet technology investors who could fund its next product.

Altwy's lightweight virtualization architecture supports Intel, AMD, ARM and RISC-V hardware on a single platform, and the company says it improves hardware efficiency and lowers energy consumption. Access is aimed at small and midsize businesses, R&D labs and projects that are not business-critical, which the company estimates make up 80% of the market, and it says the product delivers immediate savings on energy and licensing.

The company says it is backed by the French government through Bpifrance and the France 2030 investment plan, as well as by the European Union. While it prepares Core, its enterprise product for multiple servers, it has already launched Access. Core is scheduled to launch next year.

Altwy is looking to expand from Europe into South Korea, Japan and Taiwan, markets it describes as leaders in semiconductor innovation that increasingly seek data sovereignty and lower VMware licensing costs. It is seeking IT infrastructure distributors to sell Access locally and venture capital firms interested in a European infrastructure company. Building brand visibility and local trust in Asia is its main challenge, and it says matchmaking with IT hardware distributors and contact with deep-tech investors at KES would speed up its entry.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
